title: A Fluid Has a Velocity Everywhere
mathematical_role: Expose a spatial vector field together with the distinct transport, pressure, viscosity, and incompressibility terms of the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation without implying simulation output.
learning_objective: Distinguish the four mathematical roles in the PDE and remember that a field drawing does not certify global regularity.
literal_semantics: A velocity field assigns a vector u(x,t) to each spatial point and time.
The incompressible equation separates nonlinear transport, pressure gradient, viscous diffusion, forcing, and div u = 0.
Pressure is coupled nonlocally through incompressibility.
nonliteral_semantics: The arrows are schematic and are not samples from a numerical simulation.
The plate does not assert global smoothness, uniqueness of all weak solutions, or absence of singularities.

notes: Candidate semantics are bounded by the existing documentary source; no new mathematical source is admitted by this visual operation.

renderer.version_or_environment: Python 3 standard library; deterministic SVG generator v1
reproducibility_notes: The generator uses no network, randomness, timestamps, or external data.
Repository tests compare generator output byte-for-byte with the committed SVG candidate.
Text uses ASCII mathematical notation where practical to reduce missing-glyph risk in supported render paths.

accessibility.alt_text: A schematic velocity-vector field is paired with the incompressible Navier-Stokes equation, with transport, pressure, viscosity, and divergence-free constraint labeled separately.
accessibility.long_description: The left panel shows a schematic spatial vector field. The right panel writes the PDE and labels nonlinear transport, pressure, viscosity, and incompressibility separately. A claim-boundary panel states that the image is not simulation output and does not prove global smoothness.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: The plate faithfully separates the roles of the principal terms in the incompressible Navier-Stokes equation.

supersession_reason: Replace content-poor or metaphor-compressed predecessor with a literal, domain-bounded teaching representation.
